candidates: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the provider for KeyStore.getDefaultType() (typically SUN/SUNJSSE), not a Bouncy Castle provider, causing callers expecting BC-only algorithms to fail at runtime

readInteger() calls readLength() and passes result to read(int length), but readLength() returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding, causing read(-1) to throw NegativeArraySizeException instead of a checked IOException

readInteger() only checks that the low 5 bits equal 2, so it accepts context-specific, application, or private tags with tag number 2 as valid INTEGERs instead of validating that the tag is universal (bit 6 and 7 both zero)
readSequence() stops reading once the declared sequence length is consumed and silently ignores any trailing bytes in the input instead of rejecting malformed input with trailing garbage

getPemUtils() unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException, so any caller using CryptoProvider#getPemUtils() with AuthzClientCryptoProvider crashes at runtime when attempting to decode or encode PEM material
